title: Tenant safeguard registry and deterministic fallthrough scheduler
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a tenant-scoped safeguard registry plus a deterministic fallthrough scheduler to provide predictable, auditable circuit behavior across model/dependency/tenant dimensions. The registry stores per-entity trip policies, hysteresis windows, and canonical fallback mappings (eg: model-variant -> cached-response | regional-redirect | lower-quality-quantized-variant). The scheduler must ensure deterministic ordering when multiple fallbacks are possible, avoid amplification (blackhole) when fallbacks saturate downstream, and provide hooks for dry-run and canary evaluation. The feature integrates with the serving runtime for fast short-circuiting and with Console for per-tenant SLO dashboards and rollout controls.
acceptance_criteria: Registry schema defined and persisted in config store with migration plan
API endpoints to query/update per-tenant trip policy implemented and behind RBAC
Deterministic scheduler implemented in runtime to pick first-available safe fallback according to policy, with clear tie-break rules
Hysteresis and cooldown windows applied so once a tenant trips, rejoin probes follow configured backoff
Blackhole mitigation: scheduler tracks fallback utilization and enforces backpressure routes (eg: queue-to-escrow, reject-with-grace) when downstream fallback path is >80% utilized
End-to-end tests and simulation harness validate behavior under traffic spikes with at least 3 scenarios: regional outage, model slow-down, and dependent-service degradation
Console UI surfaces per-tenant active-breaker state, last-fallback-chosen, and SLO impact; alerts emit when 5xx uplift or latency breach triggered by fallback logic
Canary rollout plan documented and executed for 5 internal tenants with rollback criteria
updates: 2026-03-10 — Initial ticket filed after oncall incident where tenant B experienced cascading failure when primary model degraded; observed uncontrolled fanout to fallback causing downstream overload. Proposal drafted to centralize per-tenant policies and deterministic selection logic.

2026-03-11 — Spike simulation prototype complete (python harness) showing two failure modes: (A) fallback thundering when multiple tenants choose same low-cost model variant, (B) inconsistent rejoin causing oscillation. Added blackhole mitigation and global fallback-utilization tracking to design.

2026-03-12 — Design review with Runtime and Console teams. Key decisions: use existing config-store (Postgres) for registry, expose REST-config API + internal gRPC for runtime, implement hysteresis using exponential backoff windows, and add a lightweight escrow queue per-tenant for short-term bursts. Runtime to emit new metrics: fallback_choice, fallback_utilization_pct, breaker_state_change.

2026-03-13 — PR opened for registry schema and REST endpoints (github.com/redwood-inference/rbac-config/pull/482). Drafted migration script; raised question about multi-region replication latency — opting for async replication with leader election in control plane (trade-off: slightly stale policies vs lower operational complexity).

2026-03-14 — Implemented deterministic tie-breaker: (1) tenant-specified preference list, (2) model-variant least-recently-used score, (3) region affinity, (4) fallback-cost score. Began integration testing with runtime feature flag 'deterministic-fallback-v1'. Observability hooks added to metrics pipeline; dashboards skeleton created in Console-Canary space.
Next steps: complete unit tests for scheduler, run chaos scenarios in staging, and start canary rollout to internal tenants. Coordinate with Compliance for RBAC audit before customer rollout.
